rule.title: Project conventions for application code
rule.rule:
Application code follows the conventions in AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md. Four of them are checked on every pull request, and each is its own finding:

1. Configuration. Application code must not read process.env directly. Read configuration through the typed config or env module, so every value is validated once at startup, has a documented default, and can be replaced in tests without mutating the process environment.

2. Logging. Never call console.log, console.error, console.warn or console.debug in application code. Use the structured logger, so every line carries the request context and reaches the log pipeline with a level and fields instead of free text.

3. Errors. Do not throw the generic Error class. Throw a domain-specific error type (an existing one, or a new subclass next to the code that raises it), so callers can discriminate failures with instanceof and the API layer can map each to the right status code.

4. Types. Do not use the TypeScript any type, neither as an annotation nor as an `as any` cast. Use a concrete type, or unknown with narrowing at the boundary where the value enters, so type errors surface at compile time instead of in production.

Tests, fixtures and generated files are out of scope. A finding names which of the four conventions the line breaks.

items.title: No direct process.env reads in application code
items.spec:
WHAT: Application code must not read process.env directly.
HOW: Added lines containing `process.env` property access (e.g., `process.env.PORT`, `process.env['API_KEY']`), destructuring from `process.env`, or passing `process.env` as a value, outside tests, fixtures, and generated files.

detector.reason: A single added line containing a process.env read is itself the violation, detectable by one regex over the line's code content.

items.title: No console.log/error/warn/debug calls in application code
items.spec:
WHAT: Never call console.log, console.error, console.warn, or console.debug in application code.
HOW: Added lines invoking any of these console methods (e.g., `console.log(`, `console.error(`), outside tests, fixtures, and generated files.

detector.reason: A single added line invoking one of the forbidden console methods is self-evidently a violation, detectable with high precision by a one-line regex.

items.title: Do not throw generic Error in application code
items.spec:
WHAT: Do not throw the generic Error class; throw a domain-specific error type instead.
HOW: Added lines with `throw new Error(` or `throw Error(` outside tests, fixtures, and generated files.

detector.reason: A single added line throwing the generic Error class is matched directly by `throw new Error(` / `throw Error(`; test and generated files are excluded by the engine's path scoping, not by the regex.

items.title: No `any` type annotations in application code
items.spec:
WHAT: Do not use the TypeScript `any` type as an annotation (variable, parameter, return type, generic argument, or array element type).
HOW: Added lines containing `: any`, `<any>`, `any[]`, `Array<any>`, or similar `any` type positions, outside tests, fixtures, and generated files.

detector.reason: A single added line carries the verdict: `: any`, `<any>`, `any[]`, `| any`, `as any`, or `= any` in a TypeScript type position is detectable with word-boundary precision, though the engine cannot encode the rule's test/fixture/generated-file exclusions.

items.title: No `as any` casts in application code
items.spec:
WHAT: Do not use the TypeScript `as any` cast.
HOW: Added lines containing `as any` outside tests, fixtures, and generated files.

detector.reason: A single added line containing an `as any` cast is itself the violation, so a line-level regex detects it without further context.

pr.title: feat(ai-builder): Dual-tenant LangSmith reads for Instance AI evals (no-changelog)
pr.body:
## Summary

Dual-tenant LangSmith **reads** for Instance AI evals, for the US→EU migration. While EU builds volume we keep sourcing seed traces from the US tenant — review them, create eval cases, and replay/run them — without disrupting EU. This is dual-tenant **reads**, single-tenant (EU) **writes**: run telemetry is untouched and stays on EU.

A case selects its read tenant via a new optional `seedThread.endpoint`:

- `data/workflows/schema.ts` + `harness/langsmith-seed.ts`: add `seedThread.endpoint` (+ `SeedThreadRef.endpoint`); `ambientLangSmithConfig()` → `configFor(endpoint?)` resolves `{apiUrl, apiKey}` by host — home key for the home host, `LANGSMITH_API_KEY_US` for the US host; an unknown/unkeyed host **throws** rather than silently reading EU. Discovery deps are built per ref-tenant, preserving cross-workspace auto-discovery within the chosen tenant.
- **Omitted `endpoint` ⇒ the home (EU) tenant**, so existing cases are byte-identical and EU is zero-change. Sunset: when US drains, stop emitting the endpoint and drop the secondary key — no leftover.
- The **write path** (`cli/index.ts` `new Client()` + builder-telemetry) is untouched → results always land on EU.
- **No CI change**: seeded / US-sourced cases are `datasets: ["seeded"]`, off the PR/full suites, so CI never pulls a US trace and needs no new secret. The US key (`LANGSMITH_API_KEY_US`) is local-only (`.env.local`) for now. Home `LANGSMITH_ENDPOINT` stays explicitly EU (the SDK default endpoint is US).

The second commit folds in two unrelated cleanups from the `--source langtracer` review: the exported-case normalizer now whitelists to the schema's key set (robust vs `.strict()`), and the mcp-manifest builder reuses the canonical `ConversationTurnSchema` enum.

**Cross-repo contract:** `seedThread.endpoint` is emitted by LangTracer — companion PR n8n-io/lang-tracer#25.

## How to test

- `pnpm --filter @n8n/instance-ai typecheck` clean; **710 eval vitest green** (`configFor` resolution, schema `endpoint` acceptance, normalizer whitelist); eslint + biome clean.
- Live: run a seedThread case with `seedThread.endpoint: "https://api.smith.langchain.com"` against a real US thread, with `LANGSMITH_API_KEY_US` set in `.env.local`; the harness reconstructs from US while results write to EU. _This live US reconstruct is the remaining check before un-drafting._

## Related Linear tickets, Github issues, and Community forum posts

https://linear.app/n8n/issue/TRUST-217

## Review / Merge checklist

- [x] I have seen this code, I have run this code, and I take responsibility for this code.
- [x] PR title and summary are descriptive. ([conventions](../blob/master/.github/pull_request_title_conventions.md))
- [ ] [Docs updated](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n-docs) or follow-up ticket created.
- [x] Tests included.
- [ ] PR Labeled with `Backport to Beta`, `Backport to Stable`, or `Backport to v1` (if the PR is an urgent fix that needs to be backported)

commit.message:
feat(ai-builder): Dual-tenant LangSmith seed reads for evals (no-changelog)

Read a seed trace from either the home (EU) tenant or a secondary (US) source
during the US->EU migration, selected per case by a new `seedThread.endpoint`.
`configFor(endpoint?)` maps host->key via env (home key for the home host,
LANGSMITH_API_KEY_US for the US host) and throws on an unknown/unkeyed host
rather than silently reading the wrong tenant. Discovery deps are built per
ref-tenant, preserving cross-workspace auto-discovery within the chosen tenant.
The write path (run telemetry) is untouched and stays on EU.

Relates to https://linear.app/n8n/issue/TRUST-217

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

refactor(ai-builder): Harden langtracer case normalize + mcp-manifest types (no-changelog)

Two follow-ups from the --source langtracer review:

- normalize.ts now whitelists an exported case to the schema's accepted keys
  (WORKFLOW_TEST_CASE_KEYS) instead of blacklisting prompt/scenarios. n8n's
  schema is `.strict()` and the loader aggregates errors, so any stray key
  LangTracer attaches (id, name, suiteId, timestamps, ...) fails the whole
  suite load; whitelisting the allowed set is robust where blacklisting is not.
- build-mcp-manifest.ts reuses the canonical `ConversationTurnSchema` (the
  'user' | 'assistant' enum) at testCaseSchema + a `ConversationTurn` type at
  buildOne/casesBySlug, instead of a looser inline { role: string; text }.

Relates to https://linear.app/n8n/issue/TRUST-217

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
